short: The Anglo-American invasion of French North Africa, marking the first major US combat operation in the European theatre.
full:
On 8 November 1942, Allied forces launched simultaneous amphibious landings in Morocco and Algeria, territories controlled by the collaborationist Vichy French government. The goal was to clear Axis forces from North Africa, secure the Mediterranean, and open a second front to relieve pressure on the Soviet Union. The landings met with mixed resistance from Vichy French defenders before local ceasefires were agreed.

The success of the operation prompted Germany to occupy the remainder of metropolitan France and rush reinforcements to Tunisia. The campaign provided crucial combat experience for American troops and commanders, while effectively trapping Axis forces in North Africa between the advancing Americans in the west and the British Eighth Army in the east. The resulting Allied victory in Tunisia cleared the way for the invasion of Southern Europe.
